data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes only when the subject's guard and the test's failure channel share an observable vocabulary; the 3-of-26 result marks the boundary of that shared vocabulary, and the banding 4/4 to 6/7 is the per-module size of the shared surface.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a guard and a test could constrain the same subject while observing disjoint vocabularies, the shared-vocabulary requirement would be false.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a surviving mutation's observable signature were demonstrably inside the test's vocabulary, the boundary claim would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the banding 4/4 to 6/7 did not correlate with any measurable vocabulary overlap, the mechanism would lack support.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Guards that check declared data share a vocabulary with tests that observe declared data; guards that check declared data but face added behaviour do not. The 3 survivors are exactly the mutations whose observable signature lies outside the shared vocabulary, so the test cannot constrain them. Compile.py's 1/9 and the ordinarily-guarded modules' 4/4 to 6/7 are the sizes of their respective shared surfaces.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
